issues.title: Figma MCP enabled but OAuth authentication unavailable
issues.description: Codex listed figma-temp and figma-primary as enabled, but neither produced a ready MCP client and the UI reported authentication failure.
issues.root_cause: A remote MCP entry being enabled does not perform OAuth login. Both servers were correctly configured but remained in the Not logged in state; the Codex App did not complete the explicit login flow.
issues.solution: Use the official Codex CLI against the shared config: run `codex mcp login figma-temp` and `codex mcp login figma-primary`, completing each browser authorization with the intended Figma account.
issues.verification: `codex mcp list` reports both Figma servers as enabled with Auth=OAuth. A fresh Codex App session is still required to expose their tools, and account separation must be checked with account-exclusive test files.
issues.prevention: After adding an OAuth HTTP MCP, check `codex mcp list`; if it says Not logged in, run `codex mcp login <server-name>` before restarting the client. Never equate enabled with authenticated.

issues.title: Two Figma MCP servers reused the same browser identity
issues.description: Both figma-temp and figma-primary authenticated successfully, but their whoami calls returned the same temporary-account identity.
issues.root_cause: The second browser OAuth flow reused the Figma account already signed in to the default browser. Separate MCP server names isolate stored credentials, but they do not choose different browser identities automatically.
issues.solution: Log out only figma-primary, switch the default browser to the long-term Figma account, then run `codex mcp login figma-primary` again. Leave figma-temp credentials unchanged.
issues.verification: After restarting the Codex App, parallel whoami calls confirmed figma-temp and figma-primary have different emails and the expected account prefixes. The temporary account handle is Ran; the long-term account handle is zju.
issues.prevention: Before authorizing a second server for the same OAuth endpoint, switch the browser to the intended account. Verify both identities with whoami in fresh clients before creating canonical assets.

issues.title: MiniMax image prompt exceeded the API character limit
issues.description: The first approved v2 China-region image request returned HTTP 200 with MiniMax status 2013 because the combined prompt exceeded the image API limit. No image or provenance sidecar was created, and key2 was not selected.
issues.root_cause: The approved positive and negative Markdown blocks produced a 2018-character API prompt. The image API requires the prompt to be shorter than 1500 characters, but the local manifest builder and execution plan validated section presence without validating the final combined length.
issues.solution: Completed Step 7.4a: add a tested preflight limit of at most 1499 characters before credential or network work. Remaining: compress the approved wording without changing the generated/native layer boundary, obtain user approval for the revised text, and then run one explicit recovery request.
issues.verification: Local contract verified: `node --test scripts/design/minimax-client.test.mjs scripts/design/prompt-manifest.test.mjs scripts/design/generate-minimax-image.test.mjs` passes 23/23, including 1499 accepted and 1500 rejected before credential/network work. Pending: the approved prompt must measure at most 1499; the recovery request must either produce the versioned asset or stop on the next official error without automatic retry.
issues.prevention: Treat provider payload limits as local API contracts. Validate the final serialized prompt, not only its source sections, before loading credentials or making paid requests.
